Protecting Our Schools

Security window film is a critical component of a comprehensive school safety plan, designed to delay intruders and save lives.

A Critical Layer of Protection for Educational Facilities

In an era where school safety is a paramount concern, hardening a school's most vulnerable points—its windows and glass doors—is a critical and proactive step. Security window film is a proven, effective, and widely recommended solution for schools of all sizes. By delaying an intruder's ability to enter a school, security film buys precious time for faculty to initiate lockdown procedures and for law enforcement to arrive and neutralize the threat.

The 'Time is Life' Principle

In any active threat situation, time is the most critical asset. Security film's primary role is to provide time.

  • Intruder Delay: An attacker expecting to breach a glass door in seconds will be met with a barrier that is incredibly difficult to defeat. The minutes it takes to try and get through the filmed glass are minutes that can be used to lock doors, shelter students, and coordinate a response.
  • Deterrent: The unexpected resistance can frustrate and confuse an attacker, potentially causing them to abandon their attempt on a particular entry point or on the school altogether.
  • Blast and Accident Protection: The same film that deters intruders will also protect students and staff from injuries caused by flying glass in the event of a natural disaster, explosion, or everyday accident.

Implementing School Security Film

A comprehensive school safety plan involves layering security measures. We recommend applying security film to all ground-floor glass, particularly at the main entry vestibule and other primary access points. We use heavy-gauge films (8 mil or thicker) combined with an attachment system for maximum effectiveness.

We work with school districts and administrators across Arizona to design and implement security film solutions that meet their specific safety goals and budgets. Funding for these upgrades is often available through state and federal school safety grants.

Frequently Asked Questions

Has security film been proven effective in school safety scenarios?

Yes. There are numerous documented cases where security film has successfully delayed intruders, providing the critical time needed to initiate lockdowns and save lives. It is recommended by the Department of Homeland Security and many other safety organizations as a key retro-fit security upgrade.

Can you add a one-way privacy effect to the security film?

Yes, combination films are available that provide both security and one-way privacy. This can help to obscure the view into a classroom from the hallway, adding another layer of protection for students during a lockdown.

How is this type of project funded?

Many school districts are able to secure funding for security film installations through federal programs like the STOP School Violence Act grants, as well as various state and local safety grants. We can provide information to assist in your grant application process.
